Can a rival buy your brand name on Amazon? Kent has sued Amazon, alleging that "KENT" is sold as an advertising keyword. Shoppers searching for Kent purifiers are shown rivals' products first. The case asks whether a marketplace can profit from selling a well- known brand name to its competitors. CS(COMM) 1145/2026 Justice Tejas Karia Next hearing: 8 Dec 2026 Adv. Ashwani Kumar · Advocate | Data Privacy & Technology Law 01 / 08

HOW KEYWORD ADS WORK The brand name you never see 1 A seller bids on the keyword "KENT" in the platform's sponsored-products programme. 2 A shopper searches for "KENT" to find a Kent water purifier. 3 A rival's product appears at the top, marked "Sponsored". 4 The platform earns each time someone clicks. The word "KENT" may never appear in the ad. That is why courts call it "invisible use" and have had to decide whether it counts as use of a trademark at all. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 02 / 08

PRECEDENT 1 · DIVISION BENCH · 10 AUG 2023 Google v. DRS Logistics ✓ It is "use": using a mark as a keyword to trigger ads is use "in advertising" under the Trade Marks Act, even if the mark is never shown. ✗ But not infringement per se: there must be confusion, unfair advantage, dilution or harm to the mark. ! No safe harbour: Google actively recommended and promoted trademarks as keywords, so it was not a passive intermediary. The case began because searches for "Agarwal Packers and Movers" showed competitors' ads. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 04 / 08

Hindware v. Grohe & Google "Google was not neutral but an active commercial participant." Delhi High Court, Hindware Ltd. v. Grohe India Pvt. Ltd. 1 Invisible keyword use is use in advertising (Sections 29(6)(d) and 29(8)). 2 Google's Keyword Planner suggested the brand, auctioned it and earned per click, so there was no safe harbour. 3 Trademarks protect a brand's investment and advertising value, not just its origin. Google has appealed; the Division Bench issued notice. Some read Hindware as going further than DRS. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 08

For brands, sellers and platforms B Brands: search your own name on marketplaces, record what appears, and keep the evidence, the way Kent did with its video. S Sellers: bidding on a rival's well-known mark is now a real litigation risk. Generic terms like "RO water purifier" are safer. P Platforms: trademark keyword policies and fast complaint handling matter, because "we're just an intermediary" is getting harder to argue. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 08

Keyword ads aren't wrong in themselves. Selling a well- known brand's name to its rivals may be. DRS got the balance right: keyword ads are lawful unless they confuse buyers or take unfair advantage of a mark's reputation. For a well-known mark like KENT, on a platform that profits from every click, that line is easier to cross. Adv.
